transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~38 min
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramirez (Redwood) — Dr. Emily Park, Jordan Lee, Aisha Khan (Sunnyside Clinic)
Recording: yes

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Diego is our solutions engineer. Quick intro, then we'll jump into the model catalog demo.
[00:09] Dr. Emily Park: Hi Maya, thanks. We have about 35 - 40 minutes. Jordan will lead the technical questions. Aisha is here for security.
[00:16] Jordan Lee: Yep, thanks. Main goal: we want to see how you pick open models for our appointment summarization pipeline and get numbers on latency / cost. Also compatibility with our on-prem GPU fleet.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Perfect. Diego, do you want to share screen and open the catalog?
[00:31] Diego Ramirez: Yep sharing now. Great — so this is Redwood Console -> Model Catalog. You'll see curated open models, performance profiles, and a compatibility matrix on the right.
[00:44] Diego Ramirez: The catalog has filters: task type (chat/generation/embedding), sequence length, quantization support (fp16, int8/llm-int8), and GPU compatibility (A100/H100/T4). We also surface our benchmark metrics: median latency, 95th p99, throughput for batching, and a cost estimate per 1k tokens.
[01:02] Jordan Lee: Nice. For our use case we care about 512 token summaries, single-turn inference, and p99 latency under 400ms ideally. What model should we be looking at?
[01:12] Diego Ramirez: For 512 tokens, the catalog recommends a few variants — a 7B int8-quant model that's optimized for low-cost throughput and a 13B fp16 variant when you need higher quality and lower latency on H100. You can see the benchmark row — it's noisy because network conditions change but gives a baseline.
[01:33] Aisha Khan: Quick security question: are these benchmarks run on hosted infra? How do they differ if we run Redwood Private in our VPC?
[01:40] Maya Chen: Good question. Benchmarks shown are measured on our hosted clusters (Redwood Dedicated baseline hardware). For private deployments we provide a compatibility matrix and kernel tuning guide; performance varies by GPU and interconnect. We recommend we run a short POC on your hardware to get exact numbers.
[01:57] Jordan Lee: Can you show the compatibility matrix?
[02:00] Diego Ramirez: Sure — pull that up. So here columns are model family, quantization support, tokenizer variants, and supported kernels. Rows show tested hardware: A100, H100, Gaudi (if applicable), and CPU for small models. There's also notes for sequence-length scaling.
[02:18] Diego Ramirez: For example, this 7B int8 entry lists A100 as "validated" with throughput numbers ~120 tokens/sec on a single A100 at batch size 8 and median per-token latency ~35ms in our test harness. On H100 the same model at batch 4 shows ~200 tokens/sec and lower p50 latency.
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Those numbers are promising. Are those token numbers including tokenization and post-processing?
[02:41] Diego Ramirez: Our benchmarks include model forward pass and decode — tokenization is measured separately and adds a few ms depending on tokenizer. We can include end-to-end lat numbers in the POC.
[02:49] [Speaker 1]: uh-huh
[02:52] Dr. Emily Park: What about cost? How do you estimate cost per 1k tokens?
[02:57] Maya Chen: We estimate cost based on GPU cost and effective throughput. In the catalog each model has a "estimated cost per 1k tokens" computed from our hosted pricing and measured throughput. For dedicated or private deployments, cost will differ — Redwood Optimize provides suggestions (batching, cache, quant profiles) to reduce unit costs.
[03:13] Jordan Lee: Does Redwood Optimize automatically pick quantization profiles? We have concerns about quality regressions.
[03:19] Diego Ramirez: Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles per workload and can run evals against your prompt set to detect regressions. It's not fully automatic without your sign-off — you can preview expected quality delta on a holdout prompt set.
[03:32] Aisha Khan: Security again: KMS integration? SSO? Audit logs?
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes — private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM, SAML SSO for console access, RBAC, and audit logs with retention options. Hosted also supports envelope encryption and SOC 2 compliance; we'll share our security pack after the call.
[03:50] Jordan Lee: Good. Can you show a sample benchmark detail for the 13B fp16 model?
[03:55] Diego Ramirez: Opening the detail — here are run conditions: sequence length 512, batch sizes 1,4,8, phys GPU type H100, model compiled with cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels, KV cache behavior enabled. Results show median latency 220ms for batch1, throughput 40 tokens/sec at batch1, and cost estimate $X per 1k tokens (placeholder in UI).
[04:18] Jordan Lee: The 220ms median is okay but p99? We're sensitive to outliers.
[04:22] Diego Ramirez: p99 sits around 480ms in that run; we have options to reduce p99 using smaller max batch windows, preferential routing to low-load nodes, and prefix caching for repeated contexts.
[04:34] Dr. Emily Park: You mentioned prefix/KV cache — can we share session state across requests? Our summaries often reuse prior context for a patient session.
[04:42] Diego Ramirez: Yes — KV cache is supported and our runtime manages cache per session with TTLs. That reduces repeated decode cost significantly. In workload patterns with high context reuse we see 30-50% token compute savings.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: Nice. About tokenizer compatibility — we have some legacy tokenizers for our in-house fine-tuned models. How strict is the compatibility?
[04:59] Diego Ramirez: The catalog flags tokenizer mismatches. For many open models we support the standard tokenizers, and for custom tokenizers we provide import hooks. If there's a mismatch it's usually in encoding special tokens; we can map tokens during preprocessing. We'll note that in the compatibility matrix.
[05:14] Aisha Khan: For compliance, we need audit logs and data residency in AWS us-east-1. Is that supported?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Yes we can pin region for hosted; for stricter residency you'd likely go Redwood Dedicated or Private with a VPC deployment. We'll include region options in the quote.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: If we do Dedicated, can we reserve capacity for predictable throughput?
[05:34] Maya Chen: Absolutely, Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies and optional burst capacity. Contracts are monthly/annual commits.
[05:43] Dr. Emily Park: One more: we use a mix of small and large requests — embeddings for search and summary generation. Does the model catalog help pick separate models for each?
[05:51] Diego Ramirez: Yes, you can create "routes" in the console — embeddings route using a distilled embedder, generation route using a 7B/13B family. Catalog recommends per-task models and can simulate combined cost. There is also an A/B rollout UI to test two models in parallel.
[06:06] Jordan Lee: Can you export the compatibility matrix? We'll want to share with infra.
[06:10] Diego Ramirez: Export as CSV or JSON — I can send the CSV after the call.
[06:13] [00:06:15] Jordan Lee: Great.
[06:15] Maya Chen: I'll also attach the benchmark slides with methodology.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Ok show me how you verify quantization doesn't break our prompts.
[06:22] Diego Ramirez: In the console we have an "evals" tab where you upload a prompt set and expected outputs. Optimize runs the quantized model and reports diffs (BLEU/ROUGE or custom scoring). We show per-prompt deltas so you can triage.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: For the POC, can we run both hosted and an on-prem run? We want apples-to-apples comparison.
[06:43] Maya Chen: Yes, typical POC plan: 1) baseline hosted runs with your prompt set, 2) deploy a lightweight Private instance in your VPC or our partner region, 3) run the same harness and compare. Diego will own the POC template.
[06:58] Aisha Khan: For Private installs, what's the network model — do we ever send customer data to Redwood control plane?
[07:05] Diego Ramirez: Control plane metadata is optional; data plane stays in your VPC for Private. For our managed Private we only surface anonymized telemetry unless you opt in. We'll include docs that describe exactly what is sent.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: Can you explain the fallback policies? If a dedicated pool is saturated what happens?
[07:23] Maya Chen: We have smart routing: policy-based routing can fall back to a compatible hosted variant or a smaller quantized model. You can set cost vs latency preferences — e.g., prefer low latency up to budget, otherwise fallback to lower-cost option.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: How do you handle model variants/version pins? We maintain a pinned -01 model we tested.
[07:43] Diego Ramirez: You can pin model versions per-route in the console. Rollouts support canary or A/B with automatic fallback on quality regressions.
[07:52] Dr. Emily Park: Any gotchas for sequence length? Our notes can go to 1k tokens for long visit notes.
[07:58] Diego Ramirez: Sequence length affects memory and kernel selection. Some quant profiles are tuned for 512 tokens; for 1k we may need different kernel choices and memory configs. The compatibility matrix shows memory footprint per model+quant.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: For hardware types, we currently have mostly A100 and one H100 dev box. Will that limit our options?
[08:18] Diego Ramirez: A100 is widely validated and should be fine for both 7B int8 and 13B fp16, H100 gives better throughput for larger models. We'll detail exact kernel recommendations in the compatibility sheet.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Can you show another example: embedding model row and cost?
[08:34] Diego Ramirez: Embedding model row — we list embedder family, vector dim, median throughput (req/sec), and normalized cost per 1k tokens. For small text embedder, we see 800 req/sec on CPU optimized instances or 3k req/sec on a single T4 depending on batch.
[08:52] Aisha Khan: Do you keep logs of requests? How long?
[08:56] Maya Chen: Audit logs are configurable — default retention 90 days, longer available as add-on. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via S3 or direct integration.
[09:06] Jordan Lee: About SLAs for dedicated — what's typical availability?
[09:09] Maya Chen: We offer SLA tiers; default dedicated is 99.9, premium goes to 99.95 with faster response windows. We'll include SLA options in the pricing doc.
[09:20] [09:20] Jordan Lee: Is there support for function/tool calling or structured outputs for summaries?
[09:24] Diego Ramirez: Yes, Redwood API supports streaming responses and function calling. You can enforce structured JSON outputs via schema hints. The console's model inspector shows examples.
[09:34] Dr. Emily Park: Can we do a quick quality check — show the eval UI and run one of our sample prompts?
[09:40] Diego Ramirez: Sure — I'm switching to the evals tab. If you upload one prompt... (pause as sample uploaded) Ok running against the 7B int8 and the 13B fp16 as side-by-side.
[09:58] [09:58] Diego Ramirez: Results: 7B int8 ROUGE-L 0.78 vs 13B fp16 0.84. There's a small hallucination case in prompt 3 on the 7B int8. Optimize flagged it as medium risk.
[10:14] Jordan Lee: That's helpful. For POC we'll want the full per-prompt diff export.
[10:19] Diego Ramirez: Exportable CSV included. I'll attach.
[10:22] Aisha Khan: Anything we should watch for in ingest — PII?
[10:25] Maya Chen: We recommend PII striping or pseudonymization prior to sending off platform for hosted. For Private deployments you can keep data completely on-prem. We'll send the data handling checklist.
[10:36] Jordan Lee: Ok let's talk timeline — we'd like to start POC next week if possible. Budget owner wants a quick cost delta for hosted vs dedicated.
[10:42] Maya Chen: If you can share the sample anonymized dataset this week we'll run baseline hosted runs and return numbers within 3-4 business days. Dedicated POC on your infra may take a bit longer to schedule.
[10:53] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.
[10:55] Maya Chen: Quick recap: 1) We'll send benchmark slides and compatibility matrix; 2) Diego will share POC template and telemetry plan; 3) we'll run hosted baseline with your prompts when you provide the dataset. Any other asks?
[11:08] Dr. Emily Park: Please include SOC2 and KMS docs, the region residency confirmation, and the CSV compatibility sheet.
[11:15] Maya Chen: Noted.
[11:17] Jordan Lee: One nit: the UI showed cost as $X placeholder — can you provide a clear SKU-based quote?
[11:22] Maya Chen: I'll include SKU pricing for token/unit and dedicated capacity tiers in the estimate.
[11:27] Aisha Khan: Also please include audit log retention options and how to forward logs to our SIEM.
[11:31] Maya Chen: Will do.
[11:33] [11:33] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[11:38] Dr. Emily Park: Thanks, bye.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker labels may be generic; some model names and acronyms slightly mis-typed (e.g., "llm-int 8"), typical of automated transcription.
